title: Trumpeters McLeod, Leonard Parker, Dan Moody and Lee Collins
summary: Trumpet players he worked with, comparing Moody to Lee Collins and noting Collins played second trumpet in the Elite band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: There was a Trump McLeod from Slidell. He used to play with a lot too. He used to work through Mississippi and he used to send for Samuel Penn and I. Thomas Parker, you ever heard of? Leonard Parker. Leonard Parker. You ever heard of Leonard Parker? Sure, George Lewis used to play with him. I know he's better too. And I knew Dan Moody. Dan Moody used to be in a band too.
He mentioned him. What kind of trumpet did he play? He was good. Something like Kid Thomas? Well, I think he was better.

Did he play like anybody in particular? No. He made a lot of fancy stuff. He was something, I don't know, he started something I think on the order of Lee Collins. He had a drive. High note man or? He had high notes too. Lee, I know, could make a lot of it. Did you ever play with Lee Collins? Lee Collins? Oh yeah, Lee Collins played the second trumpet with the band, with the elite band when I was playing with them for a while. Who did you say the trumpet player in Olympia was? The trumpet player in Olympia was? The trumpet player in Olympia was? The trumpet player in Olympia was?
